diagnostic_questions.answer: M58 failed on the unzoned text 2026-04-24T14:42:05.150515 at the first reference calibrationVector/azimuthTime. Format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff without Z/offset; fromisoformat accepts it as naive; generic _parse_time raises Sentinel1RetrievalError.

All 162 calibration-vector timestamps across six sources have the same serialization class: naive, six fractional digits, no surrounding whitespace or explicit offset. The values themselves differ; they are not identical timestamp strings.
All 162 noise-range azimuthTime values have the same serialization class and identical strict-parser rejection. Each of the six ordered lists is summarized and hashed separately.
All twelve product ADS start/stop values are naive.
All twelve calibration ADS start/stop values are naive.
All twelve noise ADS start/stop values are naive.
All 360 inspected consumed values parse as ISO datetimes, carry exactly six fractional digits, have no surrounding whitespace and no offset. No missing/empty/malformed vector timestamp found.
All 18 retrieved product/calibration/noise bodies match their M58 SHA-256 and lengths: 3 documents for each of 6 sources.

Calibration-only handling leaves the same proven rejection at noise.azimuthTime and all six ADS role/start-stop boundaries. Noise range is the next timestamp family in production order if intervening calibration guards pass. M59 does not prove those intervening guards or run the complete validator.

Observed serialization is uniform across the inspected SAFE XML timestamp families, supporting review of a single narrowly scoped metadata-time boundary rather than unrelated format exceptions. UTC meaning is not established by formatting; owner/spec review is required before any UTC interpretation rule. ADS exact frozen interval guards and vector semantics must remain distinct; generic parser must not be globally relaxed.
